records.application_route: Two-step process: submit the application file in the DAAD portal, then upload work samples through the media database using the access codes provided in the DAAD portal.
records.description: The DAAD scholarship for a one to two year Master's degree in performing arts, music and German as a foreign language funds highly qualified international students in Drama, Theatre Directing/Theatre Dramaturgy, Musicals, Performance Studies, Dance, Choreography, Music and Teaching German as a Foreign Language at a state-recognised German higher education institution or public university. The scholarship pays 992 euros per month for 10 to 24 months with travel allowance and DAAD-funded insurance; tuition fees are not financed. The application is a two-step process combining the DAAD portal with a media database upload, and can take up to seven months from submission to final decision.

not_confirmed: Exact application deadline date for the current cycle - the DAAD page does not render the current date while the portal is closed ('Currently you cannot apply for this programme')
verification.notes: Verified on the official DAAD scholarship database entry on 10 October 2026: monthly payment of 992 euros, 10 to 24 months, tuition not financed, travel allowance and DAAD insurance, two-step application process (DAAD portal plus media database work samples), up to seven months from submission to decision, applications possible between 1 June and the stated application deadline, fields of study (Drama, Theatre Directing/Theatre Dramaturgy, Musicals, Performance Studies, Dance, Choreography, Music, Teaching German as a Foreign Language). Deadline recorded as null because the page does not display the current date.

records.applicant_utility: Applicant utility (original writing for the DAAD Master's Performing Arts scholarship): for stage disciplines the practical application is a portfolio process, so plan the two steps together: the DAAD portal file must be complete and the work samples visible through the media database before the evaluation can happen, and completed files take up to seven months to reach a final decision, so start early and work backwards from your semester start. The support is 992 euros per month for 10 to 24 months with a travel allowance and DAAD-funded insurance, but tuition is not financed, so research the fee structure of the specific German performing arts schools and universities on your shortlist. Your study plan, time schedule and proposed courses need validation and approval from the supervising university lecturer, which normally means you should first secure academic admission in Drama, Theatre Directing/Dramaturgy, Musicals, Performance Studies, Dance, Choreography, Music or Teaching German as a Foreign Language and then attach the scholarship application to that existing admission plan. Document your professional stage experience explicitly, since it is an eligibility element in addition to the degree results.

records.programme_name: Heinrich Böll Foundation Scholarship (Scholarship for German and International Students)
records.provider: Heinrich-Böll-Stiftung (funded by BMBF and the AA)
records.deadline_note: Spring 2027 round: application portal opens 15 January 2027 and closes 1 March 2027. Fall 2027 round: portal opens 15 July 2027 and closes 1 September 2027.
records.application_cycle: Two rounds per year: 15 January - 1 March (spring) and 15 July - 1 September (fall)
records.status_note: Applications for the spring 2027 round open on 15 January 2027 and close on 1 March 2027 (the fall 2027 round runs 15 July - 1 September 2027). The Association for the Support of Democracy (funded by BMBF) and the scholarship track supported by the Foreign Office (AA) have different selection processes and application content.
records.tuition_coverage_note: Reimbursement of tuition fees in Germany of up to 10,000 euros per year is available as an optional component for all scholarship holders.

records.application_route: Apply through the online application portal during the spring round (15 January - 1 March) or the fall round (15 July - 1 September), following the guidelines for the applicable track (AA or Association for the Support of Democracy).
records.description: The Heinrich Böll Foundation Scholarship for German and international students supports study and research in two tracks: the Association for the Support of Democracy, funded by BMBF, and a track supported by the Foreign Office (AA). The AA master's track grants a base scholarship of 992 euros per month plus a health insurance allowance of up to 100 euros per month, while the doctoral track grants 1,500 euros per month plus up to 200 euros. All scholarship holders can receive reimbursement of tuition fees in Germany of up to 10,000 euros per year, fixed fringe benefits of 38 euros per month and family/child allowances. Applications are accepted twice a year, 15 January - 1 March and 15 July - 1 September.

not_confirmed: Maximum funding periods by level of study - the scholarship page shows the funding-period overview by level and scholarship type but the exact semesters per level were not published in machine-readable form on the financial support page
verification.notes: Verified on the official Heinrich Böll Foundation pages on 10 October 2026: AA master's base scholarship 992 euros per month plus health insurance allowance up to 100 euros, AA doctoral base scholarship 1,500 euros per month plus health insurance allowance up to 200 euros, tuition-fee reimbursement up to 10,000 euros per year in Germany, fixed fringe benefits of 38 euros per month, family/child allowances, two application rounds (15 January - 1 March and 15 July - 1 September), all nationalities, non-EU applicants study in Germany, no medicine applicants, German certificates required unless study is in English, two separate tracks funded by BMBF and the AA.

records.applicant_utility: Applicant utility (original writing for the Heinrich Böll Foundation Scholarship): the foundation mixes money with a values screen, so plan for both - your file is assessed on commitment to green politics and the foundation's values, interest in study and social responsibility, and readiness for full-time study, alongside academic criteria. The money itself is concrete: for the AA master's track a base scholarship of 992 euros per month plus a health insurance allowance of up to 100 euros, or 1,500 euros plus up to 200 euros at doctoral level, with tuition-fee reimbursement in Germany of up to 10,000 euros per year, 38 euros of monthly fringe benefits and family/child allowances. Watch the two entries per year - 15 January to 1 March and 15 July to 1 September - and apply through the track that matches your funding situation (BMBF-funded Association for the Support of Democracy versus the Foreign Office AA track), since the selection content differs. Language is a practical barrier: unless your study is in English, the German certificates specified in the guidelines are required, so if you plan to study in English, keep credible proof that the programme is English-taught. Medical applicants are excluded, so pick a different funding route early if that is your field.
